Welcome to DeptfordPark Primary School
Welcome to Deptford Park. We are a warm, welcoming and inclusive school at the heart of our local community.
We are a one-form entry primary school, with a 40-place unit for children with Severe Learning Difficulties, The Constellation. We are proud to be a place where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive.
Through high-quality teaching, strong relationships and a nurturing environment, we help our pupils grow into confident, curious and resilient learners who enjoy coming to school and are proud of their achievements.
We hope our website gives you a glimpse of what makes Deptford Park such a special place to learn and grow. If you would like to arrange a visit, please contact the school office as we would be delighted to welcome you.
Cat Washbrook, Headteacher

Deptford Park Primary SchoolThe World in Our School
Values, Vision, Ethos
Vision – All children will leave Deptford Park having achieved their full potential as independent, resilient and curious learners, who are ready for the next stage in their learning journey.
Values – Our values drive all that we do at Deptford Park:
Integrity – being honest and trustworthy, and always trying to do the right thing, even when it is difficult.
Kindness – being kind to others, being a good friend and being helpful.
Respect – showing care and consideration for ourselves, other people and the things around us.
Leadership – using our actions, words, and attitude to inspire others and make a positive difference.
Resilience – having the courage to keep trying, even when things are hard, and having strategies to bounce back if something doesn’t go our way.
Sustainability – taking care of the Earth by making responsible choices today so there is enough for everyone tomorrow.

Deptford Park Primary SchoolThe World in Our School
Welcome to Deptford Park Primary School
Deptford Park Primary School is a warm, welcoming and inclusive school at the heart of our local community. We are proud to be a place where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive.
We believe that every child can succeed. Through high-quality teaching, strong relationships and a nurturing environment, we help our pupils grow into confident, curious and resilient learners who enjoy coming to school and are proud of their achievements.
As well as our mainstream classes for children aged Reception to Year 6, we are proud to have a 40-place Unit for children with Severe Learning Difficulties as part of our school. More information about this can be found here.
Our rich and engaging school curriculum provides children with opportunities to develop their knowledge, discover their talents and build the skills they need for the future. We celebrate the diversity of our community and are proud of our school motto, “The World in Our School,” which reflects the many cultures, languages and experiences that make our Deptford Park community so special. Our values of Integrity, Kindness, Respect, Leadership, Resilience and Sustainability underpin everything we do.
We know that children achieve their best when school and home work together. Strong partnerships with parents and carers are central to our success, and we work closely with families to support every child’s learning, wellbeing and personal development.
We hope our website gives you a glimpse of what makes Deptford Park such a special place to learn and grow. If you would like to arrange a visit, we would be delighted to welcome you. Please contact us at info@deptfordpark.lewisham.sch.uk.
Cat Washbrook, Headteacher

French
At Deptford Park, we believe that learning a modern foreign language should be enjoyable and accessible for every child.
Children learn the French language and explore French culture, while developing an international outlook, in a fun, engaging, and inclusive learning environment. Learning French helps children to develop their communication skills and deepen their understanding of how language works, enhancing their grammar knowledge and preparing them for the challenges of the secondary school curriculum.
French is intended as a gateway to inspire children to study foreign languages and to develop a curiosity about the cultures and traditions of other countries. Through learning French, children gain greater confidence, broaden their cultural awareness, and develop an appreciation of the diverse world around them.
How do children learn French at Deptford Park?
At Deptford Park, Modern Foreign Languages is taught through the CGP Salut! scheme, which provides a structured and progressive framework for language learning. The scheme ensures coverage of key knowledge and skills through regular practice and planned opportunities for retrieval, enabling pupils to revisit prior learning and embed new vocabulary and language structures over time. This cumulative approach supports pupils in developing confidence, resilience and increasing independence as language learners, while also providing appropriate challenge as their understanding grows.
Pupils participate in a weekly program of learning that includes a balance of speaking, listening, reading and writing activities. Throughout Key Stage 2, children develop key language skills through lessons that focus on listening and responding, building vocabulary, understanding simple grammar and using language for real purposes. By the time they move on to secondary school, pupils leave with a positive attitude towards languages and a secure foundation on which to build further language learning.

PSHE & RSE
Our Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) curriculum is designed to equip children with the knowledge, skills and attitudes they need to thrive in an increasingly complex 21st-century world. Through a broad and engaging programme of learning, children explore key topics that help them make informed decisions about their health, wellbeing, safety, relationships and financial responsibilities, both now and in the future.
We want our children to feel confident and prepared when facing challenges, understanding where to seek support and how to keep themselves safe in an ever-changing society. Through PSHE, children learn the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to build positive relationships, understand and manage emotions, stay safe online and offline, develop resilience and self-esteem, make healthy choices and prepare for later life.
When children leave Deptford Park, they will do so with the knowledge, confidence and skills needed to become active, responsible and successful members of society, ready to make a positive contribution to the world around them.
How do children learn PSHE at Deptford Park?
At Deptford Park, we use the Jigsaw curriculum, a whole-school approach that supports children’s personal development, wellbeing and safety. Jigsaw brings together PSHE Education, compulsory Relationships and Health Education, emotional literacy, mindfulness, social skills and spiritual development. It is designed as a whole school approach, with all year groups working on the same theme (Puzzle) at the same time at their own level. There are six Puzzles (half-term units of work) and each year group is taught one lesson per week. All lessons are delivered in an age- and stage-appropriate way so that they meet children’s needs.

Music
At Deptford Park, we want every child to see themselves as a musician, providing opportunities to learn to sing, play an instrument and create music together.
Through music, children develop confidence, creativity, and perseverance. As their musical skills grow, so does their sense of achievement and ability to reflect on their own learning. The children have opportunities to watch and to perform live music, and through this develop confidence, cultural awareness, and a deeper appreciation of the arts.
How do children learn Music at Deptford Park?
We teach music using Charanga Music School’s scheme for the Model Music Curriculum. It follows a differentiated, spiral approach to musical learning. Within each unit of learning, children revisit existing knowledge and skills and then build upon and extend them incrementally, increasing musical confidence and being challenged to grow further as musicians.

Art & design
At Deptford Park, we ensure that Art and Design is accessible to all learners. We want every child to see themselves as an artist — confident in experimenting, exploring, and expressing their own ideas, identities and perspectives. Our curriculum celebrates the rich diversity of our school community and encourages children to communicate their experiences through creative work.
We believe that every child deserves the chance to experience the joy and wonder of the arts. Through exploring artists, stories and art forms from the British Isles and across the world, children learn how art reflects the histories, values and cultures of different communities. We aim for all pupils to develop the skills, knowledge and creativity needed to produce meaningful, personal artwork.
How do children learn Art and Design at Deptford Park?
Deptford Park follows the Kapow Primary scheme of work, which fully supports the National Curriculum and the National Society for Education in Art and Design’s progression competencies. Learning is sequenced so that skills and knowledge are revisited, practised and extended in every year group. This approach ensures that learning is cumulative, allowing children to build confidence and independence as artists.

English
At Deptford Park, we want every child to become a confident, fluent reader and writer who can express themselves clearly and creatively. English sits at the heart of our curriculum, and we provide a rich language environment where all children can thrive. Our vision is for pupils to become fully literate, develop a love of books and high‑quality literature, and read widely for pleasure.
We teach the foundations of spelling, grammar, handwriting and punctuation securely so that children have the tools they need to write well. We also nurture children’s confidence in expressing their ideas, opinions and creativity, and ensure that their identities, cultures and languages are valued and celebrated.
How do children learn Reading at Deptford Park?
Reading is central to our curriculum, and teaching is adapted so every child can make progress through shared, guided, one‑to‑one and independent reading.
We use the Little Wandle phonics programme to help children become confident, fluent readers and writers. Through daily, engaging phonics lessons, children learn to recognise letters and sounds, blend sounds to read words and develop their spelling skills. The programme provides a clear, structured progression that ensures all pupils build strong foundations in early reading. Regular assessment and targeted support help every child to achieve success, while carefully matched reading books enable them to practise and apply their phonics knowledge with confidence both in school and at home. Those who need extra help access Daily Keep Up interventions or Rapid Catch‑Up interventions.
Little Wandle has a range of useful resources on its website to support parents: For parents | Letters and Sounds.
From Year 2, children are taught specific reading skills that help them understand and think deeply about what they read. Through a wide range of books, stories and texts, they learn to discuss characters, themes and key events, as well as explore why authors choose particular words and writing techniques. These skills help children become confident, thoughtful readers who can explain and support their ideas about a text.

We place a strong emphasis on developing a love of reading. Inviting reading corners, daily story times, class authors, reading-focused assemblies and visits to the local library encourage children to enjoy books and discover new stories.

Writing is taught through a three‑week Read–Write–Edit cycle linked to a high‑quality core text that reflects our inclusive curriculum.
Grammar, spelling and handwriting are taught through our writing cycle, with the teacher explicitly modelling the skills needed to become a fluent and confident writer. In addition, the children have dedicated lessons on grammar and spelling, supported by Emile, and on handwriting.

Maths
At Deptford Park, we want every child to see themself as a mathematician — confident, curious and able to think flexibly about number, pattern and problem solving. Our aim is to equip children with a deep, long-term and adaptable understanding of mathematical concepts that they can apply throughout their lives.
We believe that Maths should be enjoyable, meaningful and empowering. Children at Deptford Park develop fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills through rich tasks, discussion and exploration. They learn to use mathematical language confidently and to make connections across different areas of learning.
How do children learn Maths at Deptford Park?
We use White Rose to ensure our learning is carefully sequenced, builds fluency and that concepts are practised routinely. Our mastery approach is inclusive and aspirational: all children are supported to move through learning in small, connected steps that build strong conceptual understanding.
Our Maths curriculum is built around the Five Big Ideas of teaching for mastery: Coherence, Representation and Structure, Mathematical Thinking, Fluency and Variation. These principles underpin every lesson and ensure that learning is accessible, challenging and deeply understood.

Religious Education
At Deptford Park, we ensure that Religious Education is inclusive, reflective and accessible for all learners. We want every child to explore beliefs, values and worldviews, and to develop their own sense of identity and belonging.
We aim for children to develop knowledge of major world religions and non-religious worldviews, alongside the ability to ask and explore big questions about life, meaning, truth and morality.
Through RE, pupils learn to reflect, discuss, analyse and evaluate different beliefs and ethical viewpoints, and communicate their ideas clearly and respectfully.
Our curriculum promotes respect, understanding and challenge of prejudice, preparing pupils to live in a diverse society and engage positively with others.
How do children learn Religious Education at Deptford Park?
Deptford Park follows the Lewisham Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education, which provides a broad, balanced and enquiry-based curriculum focused on both learning about religion and from religion.
Learning is structured through enquiry and big questions, encouraging pupils to explore concepts such as belief, identity, belonging, meaning and morality. Pupils revisit and deepen understanding over time, building knowledge progressively.
Children study a range of religions and worldviews (including Christianity and other principal faiths, alongside non-religious perspectives), reflecting the diversity of the local and global community.

We provide opportunities for first-hand experiences, including visitors, workshops and engagement with local faith communities, supporting real-world understanding.
